cli.root.short: Automatic backup of Claude data and projects to two encrypted copies
cli.root.long:
BackUpClaude saves Claude's data every hour and your projects every day to two encrypted copies: one on a local disk and one in external storage.

This is an unofficial project, not affiliated with Anthropic.

cli.password.short: Check that the repository password exists
cli.password.long:
Without options it only says whether the password is stored.
With --show it displays the password so you can copy it to paper. That works only in a terminal window: scripts and logs never get the password.

cli.backup.long:
Saves a profile to the local repository: claude is Claude's data, projects is the working folders found in transcripts and your own folders. Without --profile both run. With --dry-run the files are read and nothing is stored.
Files another program holds are listed. Exit code 1 means something is missing from the snapshot.
cli.list.long: Shows snapshots, sessions and projects. Without options it shows all three. A session Claude has already deleted shows up if the latest snapshot holds it.
cli.measure.short: Size of a profile and folders heavy with media
cli.measure.long: Walks a profile with the same exclusions as a backup and finds folders with a lot of media. Reads no file content.
cli.verify.short: Read what a snapshot really holds
cli.verify.long: Reads the file tree of the latest snapshot of a profile and compares it with the disk. Exit code 1 means something is missing or something banned got in.

cli.schedule.short: Put the automatic runs into the Windows Task Scheduler
cli.schedule.long: Creates, shows and removes the scheduled tasks: Claude's data every hour, projects every day, cleanup and check every week by default. The intervals come from the settings. The tasks run as you, without administrator rights, show no window and catch up after the computer was off.
cli.schedule.install.short: Create the tasks, or update them to match the settings
cli.schedule.remove.short: Remove the tasks, the copies stay
cli.schedule.status.short: Show the tasks as the scheduler holds them
cli.run.long: What a scheduled task runs: removes the locks of a crashed run, does the job (claude, projects, cleanup or check) at low priority and writes a line to logs/runs-YYYY-MM.jsonl.
